key_insight: Variational quantum optimization can correct strong-disorder renormalization-group approximations using shallow circuits tailored to a two-dimensional disordered Ising model.
engineering_relevance: Renormalization-group structure provides a physics-informed route to hardware-compatible circuits for simulating disordered quantum systems.
method: Adapt the emergent-coupling-based ansatz to the two-dimensional random transverse field Ising model.
Use the SDRG flow to determine circuit structure.
Optimize circuit parameters to capture correlations beyond the SDRG approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical and IQM superconducting-hardware studies report relative energy accuracies of 89% for 16 qubits with full on-device optimization and 97% for 49 qubits using pre-optimized parameters.
watch_item: The 49-qubit experiment uses pre-optimized parameters, so it does not demonstrate full variational optimization at that scale.
paper_title: Variational Corrections to Strong-Disorder Renormalization in the Two-Dimensional Random Transverse Field Ising Model on Quantum Hardware
